title: Lesson 88: Exam prep: CTA review and scenario practice
description: Tests the Review Board format and its three-clock structure, the integration and org-strategy decisions a scenario forces, the published presentation guidance, and the preparation-block time budget.

questions.question: Ridgeline Freight's on-premise ERP owns rating and billing and exposes roughly 500 API calls a day. Rating and invoice status carry an hourly tolerance. Which recommendation matches the scoring answer in this lesson?
options: Make the CRM wait on an ERP call for each invoice status change so billing is always current
Synchronize them into a read-only object on a scheduled job and batched reconciliation
Connect the two orgs through a shared integration layer and leave the org question open
Sync the full shipment list to each field device so technicians always have current data
questions.explanation: The lesson's scoring answer keeps billing authoritative in the ERP and treats rating and invoice status as reference data with an hourly tolerance, so it synchronizes them into a read-only object on a scheduled job and batched reconciliation. That choice keeps daily consumption inside the 500-call ceiling that the scenario states. Per-record callouts contradict the limit the scenario just gave you, and the org question is a scored decision rather than one to leave open.

questions.question: You have 45 minutes to present your design to a panel of CTA judges, and your decision log has resolved every open choice. Which approach follows the guidance Salesforce publishes to candidates?
options: State the technology you would buy first, then work backwards to the requirement it satisfies
Open with the architecture diagram so the panel assembles the problem for themselves
Present your recommended solutions and not options
Present every option you considered and let the judges pick the one they prefer
questions.explanation: The published guidance for candidates is to present recommended solutions and not options, to justify why the solution should be used, and to keep the solution relevant to the scenario. A menu of options reads as an unresolved design, and the exam scores a decision with its trade-off attached. Technology-first delivery also hides the requirement the decision was meant to satisfy.

questions.question: A candidate spends 140 minutes of the 180-minute preparation block polishing the system landscape diagram and reaches minute 140 with an empty numbers sheet. Which practice in this lesson addresses that failure?
options: The diagram is the artifact that eats time, so it gets a hard stop
Read the scenario once, then start drawing immediately so the picture is ready early
Skip the constraint table and rely on the decision log alone for the presentation
Present options instead of a recommendation when the clock gets tight
questions.explanation: The lesson budgets the 180 minutes in blocks precisely because the diagram is the artifact that eats time, so it gets a hard stop at minute 110. The numbers sheet is where the scenario's call limits, volumes and latency targets get checked, and an empty sheet means the arithmetic never happened. Cutting the constraint table is also wrong, because a thin constraint table is a reading problem that no amount of diagram practice fixes.
